SnowDistribution: Some icy paths, with areas of water ice present. Mixed visibility.
WeatherInfluences: Winds will be South-Easterly, initially moderate strengthening overnight to be very strong or gale force through the day. It is expected to be dry overnight and during the morning, then snowfall above around 1000 metres through the afternoon. The freezing level is expected to be around 600 metres overnight, and around 1000 metres during the day.
SnowStability: Unstable windslab will be present in sheltered areas, mainly on West through North to North-East aspects above 950 metres. During the afternoon further deposits of unstable windslab will form in sheltered areas, mainly above 1050 metres on these aspects. Weak cornices will also be present above these aspects. The avalanche hazard will be Moderate.
ObservedWeatherInfluences: After overnight snowfall, it was a showery day with snow falling above around 850 metres. Winds were moderate South-South-Easterly. The freezing level was around 900 metres.
ObservedSnowStability: Unstable windslab has been deposited in sheltered areas, mainly on West through North to North-East aspects above 950 metres. Weak cornices are forming above these aspects. The avalanche hazard is Moderate.

Comment: 2 to 4cm of snow expected, this could increase to much heavier precipitation depending on when the snowfall arrives.
WeatherInfluences: Dry overnight, before the arrival of snowfall during the day.  Fresh South winds will begin to increase overnight to become gale to storm force South-South-Easterlies during the day. The 600 metre freezing level will rise to around 1000 metres during the day.
SnowStability: During the day further unstable windslab will develop on North-West to North aspects above 950 metres. Instabilities  also on West, North-East and East aspects above the same altitude. The greatest instability will be in steep locations such as gullies, gully tops, coire rims and convexities. On these aspects, cornices will be fragile. Below this altitude and above 700 metres isolated deposits of windslab will affect wind sheltered areas. The avalanche hazard will be Considerable.
ObservedWeatherInfluences: Snow fall cleared to leave a dry day.  Gale force Southerly winds eased fresh to strong.  The freezing level was around 1000m.
ObservedSnowStability: Further unstable windslab has developed on North-West to North-East aspects above 950 metres. West and East aspects are affected by cross-loading. The greatest instability is in steep locations such as gullies, gully tops, coire rims and convexities. On these aspects, cornices are fragile. Below this altitude and above 700 metres isolated deposits of windslab are present on steep banks and burn lines.  The avalanche hazard is Considerable.
